subject: HIPAA scope & PHI boundary map — CareLane discovery follow-up
content:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Samir Patel <samir.patel@carelane.com>, security@carelane.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0500
Subject: HIPAA scope & PHI boundary map — CareLane discovery follow-up

Hi Samir / CareLane security team,

Thanks again for the time today — helpful to walk through the high-level use case for clinician triage and the places patient data touches the system. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same checklist: 

Recap from our call:
- Primary PHI elements: patient name + DOB, contact info, medical record numbers, structured lab results, and occasional uploaded PDFs with notes.
- Expected volume: low-to-moderate per-hour predictions initially (prototype cohort), with bursty periods during triage windows.
- Initial requirement: BAA and confirmation on eligible deployment models for PHI.
- Compliance posture: CareLane indicated you run internal SOC/ISO checks; you requested Redwood's SOC 2 status and a starter vendor questionnaire.

How Redwood can support (summary):
- BAA availability: We provide a standard BAA for customers handling PHI. BAAs are offered for Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with VPC peering) and Private deployments (customer-controlled network/on‑prem) as the recommended paths for regulated PHI workflows.
- Hosted API: We can contractually support specific hosted arrangements in limited cases, but for most PHI workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private so you retain network isolation and key control.
- PHI boundaries we enforce: we can map and limit token retention, disable server-side persistent logs for specific routes, and configure KV/prefix caching exclusions for PHI-bearing prompts.
- Key management: support for customer-managed KMS/HSM for Private deployments; Dedicated offers bring-your-own-key integrations in our higher-tier plans.

Requested artifacts (attached and actions):
1) Security questionnaire: I’m attaching a short vendor security questionnaire (carelane_security_questionnaire_v1.xlsx) — please fill sections A/B (attestation + dataflow) and return.
2) Dataflow diagram: please attach a redacted example of a typical request payload (or the dataflow diagram). We included a placeholder (carelane_dataflow_v1.pdf) — if you can replace that with your version, we’ll map exact controls.
3) Timing & next meetings: propose a 1-hour technical mapping call with our Solutions Engineer and Security lead on Wed Nov 4 at 10:00 AM PT to run through tokenization, storage controls, and a Dedicated pricing sketch.
4) SOC 2 status: we’ll send our SOC 2 attestation and evidence pack; please let us know if you need Type II or particular control narratives.

Deliverables from Redwood on that call:
- Deployment options matrix (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) with PHI suitability and estimated cost delta.
- Example BAA and SOW excerpt for Dedicated.
- A preliminary list of configuration knobs (KMS, data retention, caching rules).

If this aligns, please: 1) confirm the Nov 4 slot, 2) return the questionnaire with the dataflow attachment, and 3) identify your procurement/compliance owner so we can send the BAA draft.

Thanks — looking forward to continuing.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

---

On Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:17:12 -0800, Dr. Samir Patel <samir.patel@carelane.com> wrote:
> Hi Lauren / team,
>
> Thanks for the recap — that captures it well. A few clarifications from our side: 
> - PHI scope: includes patient identifiers + encounter notes + lab attachments. We may also pass insurance payer info in some workflows.
> - Preferred deployment: Security leadership prefers Dedicated (VPC, private subnet) for the POC if the cost delta is reasonable. We want to avoid hosted multi-tenant for any PHI at this stage.
> - SOC 2: CareLane requires our vendors to be SOC 2 Type II or have an explicit remediation timeline. Can you confirm Redwood’s current SOC 2 status and when you expect the next Type II report?
> - Questionnaire: attaching two files — our filled vendor questionnaire (carelane_security_questionnaire_v1.xlsx) with inline notes, and a short dataflow PDF showing where documents and images enter the system (carelane_dataflow_v1.pdf).
>
> Action items from us: we’ll send the filled questionnaire by EOD tomorrow and confirm the compliance owner (I’ll loop in Maria from procurement). Also want a short cost sketch for Dedicated vs Private before the call.
>
> Samir
